title: Add KV fragmentation workload generator (mixed-length + churn) for repeatable benchmarks
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
## Summary
Adds a new benchmark-lab workload generator that reproduces allocator fragmentation patterns we’ve been seeing in sustained decode with mixed sequence lengths + request churn. The goal is to make the compaction/eviction work measurable and repeatable across GPUs/models with a single command, and to provide a stable “fragmentation pressure” scenario for perf canary gating.

This is intentionally *not* a perfect simulation of production traffic. It’s a controllable stressor that drives:
- mixed prefill sizes (short + long prompts)
- long-lived sessions that keep KV pages pinned
- intermittent churn (cancels + short sessions) that creates holes
- burst windows that amplify tail latency sensitivity

## Why
Runtime compaction changes (ENG-4821) need a benchmark that:
- reliably increases the KV arena fragmentation ratio (vs. random traffic that sometimes doesn’t)
- makes results comparable between PRs (deterministic seeds, fixed distributions)
- emits enough per-step metadata to correlate fragmentation → p95/p99

## What’s included
- New generator: `kv_frag_churn` (name bikesheded in review; settled on `kv_frag_churn` to avoid “allocator-specific” naming).
- Distribution model:
  - Prefill length distribution: mixture model (p50 ~ 256 tokens, tail up to configurable max)
  - Session lifetime: mixture of long-lived sessions (stickiness) + ephemeral sessions
  - Cancellation rate + cancellation timing knobs (simulate “user stops generation”)
  - Burst schedule (periodic burst windows with adjustable multiplier)
- Determinism:
  - All RNG is seedable (`--seed`), and the generator logs the resolved seed/config into the run output.
  - A single run produces a `run_manifest.json` with the generator config (for copy/paste reproduction).
- Output artifacts:
  - Per-interval CSV: request rate, active sessions, cancellation count, queueing delay, latency percentiles
  - Optional “allocator snapshot marker” events for downstream ingestion (runtime can record snapshots when it sees the marker; see notes below).
- Harness wiring:
  - Added to `bench run` CLI (`bench run --workload kv_frag_churn ...`)
  - Adds baseline config preset: `--preset kv_frag_canary_v1`

## Usage
Example (staging-like pressure):
- `./bench run --model llama-3-70b --workload kv_frag_churn --preset kv_frag_canary_v1 --seed 1337 --duration 20m`

Example (more aggressive churn):
- `./bench run --model llama-3-8b --workload kv_frag_churn --prefill-max 8192 --cancel-rate 0.18 --burst-multiplier 2.5 --seed 42 --duration 10m`

## Notes / Integration points
- This PR does *not* require runtime changes to run. It can run against any runtime build.
- If the runtime exports allocator metrics (e.g. `kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio`), the benchmark will automatically record them into the CSV when present.
- There’s an optional “snapshot marker” event type that the runtime team can hook into for allocator dumps during compaction experiments (kept off by default).

## Validation
- Ran locally against A100 and L4 test rigs (sanity): generator drives fragmentation signals up under churn vs. steady-state decode.
- CI: unit tests for determinism (same seed = same event schedule), schema validation for output artifacts, and basic smoke run on the smallest model fixture.

## Follow-ups
- Add “golden” regression thresholds once we lock the perf-canary pass/fail gate (tracked in ENG-4828 / perf-canary PR).
- Once runtime compaction lands, we’ll add a companion report that highlights before/after deltas using the same seed/config.

- Runtime project epic: ENG-4821
- Perf canary scenario ticket: ENG-4828
- Related runtime PRs (context): redwood/pr-19357, redwood/pr-19371

review_conversation:
Marcus Reed (review): The generator looks good, but we need strict determinism for canary gating. Right now `time.Now()` is used as a default seed; can we force an explicit seed or at least always log the resolved seed?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated so the resolved seed is always included in `run_manifest.json` + printed to stdout. CLI still defaults to time-based seed for ad-hoc runs, but presets used by CI/perf-canary will set an explicit seed.

Sahana Iyer (review): The interval CSV schema is missing a stable header order (some columns are conditional). Can we make the header stable and leave missing metrics blank to simplify ingestion?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Done. Header order is now stable; allocator metrics columns are always present and emitted as empty when not available.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Please rename `kv_allocator_frag` to something workload-oriented; we’ll likely change allocator naming during compaction work. Also would be helpful to add a knob for long-lived session fraction.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Renamed to `kv_frag_churn`. Added `--long-lived-fraction` with preset defaults tuned to reproduce fragmentation quickly on the staging profile.

Allison Grant (review): Can we add explicit metric mapping to the output when `kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio` exists? (Even if it’s just “best effort”.)

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added a best-effort scrape for known metric names and records them in the interval CSV. Included a short doc note listing the recognized names.

CI note: First run failed due to a flaky timing assertion in determinism test on the runner; fixed by removing wall-clock tolerances and validating event sequence hashes instead. Rerun passed.

Marcus Reed (final): Approved once stable header + seed logging landed.

Merge: Squashed and merged to main.
release_notes: benchmark-lab: adds `kv_frag_churn` workload generator and `kv_frag_canary_v1` preset for reproducible KV fragmentation pressure runs; emits run_manifest + stable interval CSV outputs for perf analysis.
